title: customer.subscription.deleted webhook writes 'cancelled' to both Organization.subscription.status and SubscriptionOrg.status
description: The handler's own code comment notes this dual-write 'fixes a real prior bug' where only one of the two status fields was updated, leaving the two records disagreeing about whether the org was cancelled. Regression guard to ensure a future refactor doesn't reintroduce the single-write bug.
preconditions: Org has an active org-level Stripe subscription
steps: Trigger a customer.subscription.deleted event for the org's subscription
Read both Organization.subscription.status and the corresponding SubscriptionOrg.status after the webhook completes
expectedResult: Both fields read 'cancelled'. Neither is left stale/out of sync with the other.

title: Cancelling a pending downgrade with none scheduled stays a silent client no-op, not a surfaced error toast
description: billingService.cancelPendingChange() is called defensively in a few UI paths; the server's NO_PENDING_CHANGE code must keep being treated as success by the client so an org with nothing pending doesn't see a spurious error toast.
steps: From the UI, trigger the cancel-pending-downgrade action (e.g. via PendingDowngradeBanner's Cancel, if rendered defensively even with nothing pending)
expectedResult: No error toast/banner appears; the call completes silently as a no-op, consistent with the server's NO_PENDING_CHANGE response.

title: Unhandled/unknown Stripe event types are acknowledged 200 rather than causing a 500 that triggers Stripe retry storms
description: Any event type without a registered handler (e.g. payment_intent.succeeded, which has no handler in this codebase) must still return 200 { received:true, ignored: event.type } so Stripe doesn't interpret it as a delivery failure and retry indefinitely.
preconditions: A syntactically valid, correctly-signed Stripe event of a type with no registered handler (e.g. payment_intent.succeeded)
steps: Send this event to POST /webhooks/stripe with a valid signature
expectedResult: 200 { received:true, ignored:'payment_intent.succeeded' } and no stripe_events record is left in a 'failed' state; Stripe does not retry the delivery.
